description: Building an interactive Martian Survival Map using NASA data. Looking for passionate teammates in coding, UI/UX, data, and space exploration. Let’s innovate together!
summary: RedPath is an interactive Mars surface planning tool that helps astronauts decide where it is safe to walk. It combines NASA Mars data layers (elevation and slope, water-equivalent hydrogen as a proxy for ice, radiation, temperature and dust) onto one map. For each point it calculates a 0-100 survival score, and users can change how much each factor counts. A hazard-aware route planner then finds the shortest and the safest walking route between two points, avoiding steep terrain and low-scoring areas, and compares them on distance, EVA time, slope and radiation dose. A mission panel adds alerts and a site briefing for sites such as Jezero and Gale Crater. It addresses the challenge of giving explorers a layered, integrated view for planning a safe Marswalk.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

RedPath divides a 240 km area around a chosen Mars site (Jezero, Gale, Arcadia or Utopia) into a 96x96 grid. Each cell stores elevation, slope, water-equivalent hydrogen, radiation dose, temperature and dust opacity. These are converted into ratings and combined, with adjustable weights, into a 0-100 survival score. Cells steeper than a user-set limit are treated as impassable. An A* route planner then compares a distance-only route with a safety-weighted route and reports distance, EVA time, steepest slope, mean score and radiation dose for each.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Mission planners can see the trade-off between a short walk and a safe walk, check EVA time and radiation exposure, and choose destinations with ice access. Adjustable weights let the same tool support different mission priorities. A mission panel gives live readouts, alerts and a site briefing.

TOOLS

JavaScript, Leaflet and NASA Trek map tiles for the interface; Python with rasterio and NumPy to convert NASA rasters into grid data; GitHub Pages for hosting.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Radiation is estimated with an elevation-based model scaled to the surface dose measured by Curiosity's RAD instrument at Gale Crater (about 0.64 mSv/day); it is not measured at each point. The score thresholds, walking speed (2.5 km/h) and EVA window (8 h) are planning assumptions that mission experts should validate. The data pipeline records which layers come from NASA rasters and which are modelled, and the app shows this in its site briefing.

CREATIVITY

Most tools show data layers separately. RedPath turns them into a decision: two comparable routes that an astronaut can act on, with a score the user can tune.

SI USE

The code (index.html and build_data.py) was generated with SI assistance (Claude, by Anthropic) and reviewed by the team. The disclosure is in the code comments, page metadata and README. No NASA logos, flags or mission identifiers are used.
